text:
behind most failures — every write was rebuilding every pane:

Now the size-control tests need to account for the narrow layout hiding them:

Both are real: focus is lost after a keyboard move, and two panes each have their own inspector now.

The drag test reloads inside the not-yet-durable window. The shell needs a durability signal that doesn't depend on which panes are open:

All green. Adding coverage for the stacked layout itself:

Now the docs. `CLAUDE.md` still describes a router that no longer exists:

The sync round-trip guard says "all seven kinds" and there are now eight — it passed only because it was hardcoded:

Done. A 2x2 grid of panes, arranged out of the registry, stored in the op log.

**How it works.** `src/views/grid.ts` is the whole model: a pane is `{ page, w, h }` — an order and a span, no coordinates, because CSS grid does the packing and storing it twice invites the two to disagree. `fits()` simulates `grid-auto-flow: row dense` exactly, so a layout the model accepts is one the browser draws in two rows.

That check earned its keep immediately. **A cell count is not enough**: a 2x1 plus a 1x2 is four cells that cannot tile a 2x2 — the wide one takes a whole row and what's left is a row one cell tall. Reachable in two presses, and an area check would have put the second pane on a third row, below the fold. `canResize` refuses it, and there's a test named after it.

**Interactions.** Nav pills toggle panes open and closed. Opening one when the grid is full *makes room* rather than refusing — largest pane first, width before height — so pressing "Notes" while Todos fills the screen gives you exactly the 1x2 + 1x2 you described, in one press. Panes drag by the grip; arrow keys do the same thing from the keyboard. The nav only greys out at four 1x1 panes, when nothing can shrink further.

**The op.** Rather than teach `core/` what a pane is, there's one new variant — `{ k: 'pref', key, value }`, a named last-writer-wins register. Core learns "named value", the grid owns the shape. It has a replay test, it's in the convergence property test, and it round-trips through sync. `parsePanes` treats whatever comes back out of the log as untrusted: unknown pages, bad spans and layouts that don't fit are dropped individually, because another device may have a module this build doesn't.

**Routing is gone**, as that choice implies — `@solidjs/router` came back out of `package.json`, and `CLAUDE.md` now records why so it isn't re-added by reflex.

**Three bugs found by driving the real app**, all fixed and now covered:
- Every op rebuilt every pane. `useQuery` re-runs on any write and parsing allocates fresh objects, so `<For>` threw away all pane state — the visible symptom was an inspector that closed itself the moment you added a link with it. Split into two memos.
- The drop never landed. Reordering during a drag moves the grip's own node, the browser fires `lostpointercapture`, and the `pointerup` that would commit goes elsewhere. It looked like it worked and snapped back on reload. Drags now listen on the window.
- Keyboard moves worked exactly once — focus went with the replaced node. Now restored after the move.

I also fixed a test that had gone stale in the same direction: the sync round-trip guard asserted "all seven kinds are covered" and kept passing after the eighth was added. It compares against `OP_KINDS` now.

**Verified:** 373 unit tests, 56 e2e (4 skipped — size controls are hidden on one column, where a span changes nothing). `bun run check` and `bun run build` clean. I drove the grid in Chromium at 1240px and 412px: opened, resized, dragged, moved by keyboard, and reloaded each time.

Two costs are now written into `BACKLOG.md` rather than left implicit: the layout is a single register, so two devices rearranging concurrently means one loses their arrangement outright instead of merging; and every rearrange is an op in a log replayed from genesis, which nothing compacts yet. Nothing is committed.

text:
Sync has to keep running when the settings pane is closed — its interval and key recall live in `onMount`. Splitting the engine from the form:

Now Settings becomes a page like Calendar, and pages carry what draws them:

Now the shell — header gone, full width:

Now the styles — full width, no masthead, and an offscreen heading:

Now the sync e2e spec, which opened a panel that no longer exists:

All green. Let me look at the result:

Work is done and verified. Let me quickly handle the recurring tooling friction that was flagged.

Done — all three changes.

**Full width.** `.shell` lost its `max-width` and centring. A measure exists to keep a line of prose readable, and a grid of panes isn't prose — each pane wraps its own content, so the cap was leaving a wide screen mostly margin while the panes were the thing short of room. Body padding is down to one step so panes clear the bezel and nothing more. At 1600px the shell is 1568px wide and the calendar finally has space to be a calendar.

**Header gone.** The `lexio` title bar told nobody anything they didn't know — it's the only app on the screen — and it cost a row of height on the surface with the least of it. The nav pills are now the top of the page. One thing survives it: an off-screen `<h1>`, because a document with no heading leaves every pane's `<h2>` hanging off nothing. The skip link stays.

**Settings is a page.** It joins the nav from `pages.ts` alongside Calendar — the two pages no module owns, enumerated in one place, each carrying the component that draws it. `Page` gained a `render` field, so the grid asks "does a module own this" and otherwise draws whatever the page brought; no third special case in `Grid.tsx`.

The part that needed care: **sync must not stop when you close the settings pane.** A pane is disposable, and everything that makes sync automatic — the 60s interval, the `visibilitychange` listener, the recall of a remembered key — lived in the panel's `onMount`. So `Sync.tsx` is now two pieces: `SyncProvider` holds all the state and the engine and is mounted by the shell for the app's lifetime, and `SyncSettings` is only the controls, reading it through context. The form holds nothing, which means closing settings loses nothing — not even a half-typed passphrase. That's the exact property the old "collapsing does not throw away what is in it" test asserted, and it still asserts it, now by closing the pane instead of collapsing a panel.

I also removed the `.sync-toggle` styles, and fixed the narrow-layout `min-block-size` that was still subtracting the old body padding.

**Verified:** 373 unit tests, 56 e2e (4 skipped on the one-column project by design), `bun run check` and `bun run build` clean. Looked at it at 1600px and at 412px — no horizontal overflow, pills wrap to two rows on the phone, settings reads fine stacked.

One note recorded in `BACKLOG.md`: Settings has exactly one thing on it today, and if that list grows it wants sections rather than a second pill.

---

Separately — a piece of recurring friction worth three lines, if you want it. Twice now (this session and an earlier one) I've tried to check the narrow layout by resizing Chrome, and `resize_window` refuses any bounds under about half the screen. The working route is Playwright with an explicit viewport, which this repo is already set up for. Proposed under the existing **Testing** heading in `CLAUDE.md`:

```md
- Check narrow layouts with Playwright at an explicit viewport, not by resizing
  the browser — the resize tool refuses bounds under ~50% of the screen. The
  `mobile-chromium` project is already a Pixel 7.
```

Say the word and I'll add it; it's parked for a week otherwise. I dropped the other flagged item (`python3` retries) — those were my own typos in throwaway scripts, and no note would have prevented them.
